**Notice:** *These are NOT the problems on Exam 3. They are SIMILAR to the problems on Exam 3.* Try the problems first on the [printable practice (PDF)](Exam3_fall26_practice1.pdf), then check your work here.

**ReLU function:** $\text{ReLU}(z) = \max(0, z)$.

# Problem 1. LASSO

This is a **regression problem**: we want to predict a numeric target $y$ from two inputs, $x_1$ and $x_2$, using the data below.

| $x_1$ | $x_2$ | $y$ |
|:-----:|:-----:|:-----:|
| 1 | 0 | -2 |
| 2 | 1 | 0 |
| 3 | -2 | -1 |
| 4 | 3 | 1 |

Consider these four models:

$$
\begin{aligned}
\text{Model A:} \quad \hat{y} &= -2 + 0.5 x_1 + 0.25 x_2 \\
\text{Model B:} \quad \hat{y} &= -1.25 + 0.25 x_1 + 0.25 x_2 \\
\text{Model C:} \quad \hat{y} &= -0.5 + 0 x_1 + 0.25 x_2 \\
\text{Model D:} \quad \hat{y} &= -0.5 + 0 x_1 + 0 x_2
\end{aligned}
$$

Each model has the form $\hat{y} = w_0 + w_1 x_1 + w_2 x_2$. Its total squared loss is $L(w_0, w_1, w_2) = \sum (\hat{y} - y)^2$. LASSO adds a penalty on the size of the slopes $w_1$ and $w_2$. The best model is the one with the smallest **objective**:

$$\text{Objective} = L(w_0, w_1, w_2) + \alpha \left( |w_1| + |w_2| \right)$$

The number $\alpha$ sets how strong the penalty is. The intercept $w_0$ is not penalized.

a. Which of the four models is best when $\alpha = 0$? With $\alpha = 0$ there is no penalty, so this is the ordinary linear model.

b. Which of the four models is best when $\alpha = 4$?

c. Which of the four models is best when $\alpha = 7$?

d. Which of the four models is best when $\alpha = 10$?

e. As $\alpha$ increases, what happens to the slopes of the best model?

::: {.callout-tip}
## Solution

**Start by calculating the loss of each model.** For Model A:

| Row | $x_1$ | $x_2$ | $y$ | $\hat{y} = -2 + 0.5 x_1 + 0.25 x_2$ | $\hat{y} - y$ | $(\hat{y} - y)^2$ |
|:-----:|:-----:|:-----:|:-----:|:-----:|:-----:|:-----:|
| 1 | 1 | 0 | -2 | $-2 + 0.5 + 0 = -1.5$ | 0.5 | 0.25 |
| 2 | 2 | 1 | 0 | $-2 + 1 + 0.25 = -0.75$ | -0.75 | 0.5625 |
| 3 | 3 | -2 | -1 | $-2 + 1.5 - 0.5 = -1$ | 0 | 0 |
| 4 | 4 | 3 | 1 | $-2 + 2 + 0.75 = 0.75$ | -0.25 | 0.0625 |

Adding the last column gives $L = 0.875$. The other models work the same way:

| Model | $\hat{y}$, row 1 | $\hat{y}$, row 2 | $\hat{y}$, row 3 | $\hat{y}$, row 4 | $L$ | $\lvert w_1 \rvert + \lvert w_2 \rvert$ |
|:-----:|:-----:|:-----:|:-----:|:-----:|:-----:|:-----:|
| A | -1.5 | -0.75 | -1 | 0.75 | $0.25 + 0.5625 + 0 + 0.0625 = 0.875$ | $0.5 + 0.25 = 0.75$ |
| B | -1 | -0.5 | -1 | 0.5 | $1 + 0.25 + 0 + 0.25 = 1.5$ | $0.25 + 0.25 = 0.5$ |
| C | -0.5 | -0.25 | -1 | 0.25 | $2.25 + 0.0625 + 0 + 0.5625 = 2.875$ | $0 + 0.25 = 0.25$ |
| D | -0.5 | -0.5 | -0.5 | -0.5 | $2.25 + 0.25 + 0.25 + 2.25 = 5$ | $0 + 0 = 0$ |

**Then calculate each objective,** $L + \alpha \times (\lvert w_1 \rvert + \lvert w_2 \rvert)$. The smallest in each column is in bold.

| Model | $\alpha = 0$ | $\alpha = 4$ | $\alpha = 7$ | $\alpha = 10$ |
|:-----:|:-----:|:-----:|:-----:|:-----:|
| A | **0.875** | $0.875 + 4(0.75) = 3.875$ | $0.875 + 7(0.75) = 6.125$ | $0.875 + 10(0.75) = 8.375$ |
| B | 1.5 | $1.5 + 4(0.5) =$ **3.5** | $1.5 + 7(0.5) = 5$ | $1.5 + 10(0.5) = 6.5$ |
| C | 2.875 | $2.875 + 4(0.25) = 3.875$ | $2.875 + 7(0.25) =$ **4.625** | $2.875 + 10(0.25) = 5.375$ |
| D | 5 | $5 + 4(0) = 5$ | $5 + 7(0) = 5$ | $5 + 10(0) =$ **5** |

a. Model A is best at $\alpha = 0$, with objective 0.875. It has the smallest loss, and it uses both inputs.

b. Model B is best at $\alpha = 4$, with objective 3.5. It uses both inputs, with a smaller slope on $x_1$ than Model A.

c. Model C is best at $\alpha = 7$, with objective 4.625. It uses only $x_2$.

d. Model D is best at $\alpha = 10$, with objective 5. It uses neither input and predicts $-0.5$, the mean of $y$, for every row.

e. The slopes shrink toward 0, and they reach exactly 0.
:::

# Problem 2. Image Recognition (CNN)

A CNN takes the $5 \times 5$ grayscale image $X$ and applies the $2 \times 2$ filter $K$ (bias 0, stride 1, no padding).

$$
X = \begin{bmatrix}
1 & 0 & 3 & 3 & 0 \\
0 & 1 & 3 & 2 & 0 \\
0 & 0 & 2 & 3 & 1 \\
1 & 0 & 3 & 3 & 0 \\
0 & 0 & 1 & 2 & 0
\end{bmatrix}
\qquad
K = \begin{bmatrix} -1 & 1 \\ -1 & 1 \end{bmatrix}
$$

The convolution gives the $4 \times 4$ feature map below. Its first row is missing.

$$
\text{Feature map} = \begin{bmatrix}
\boxed{\ ?_1\ } & \boxed{\ ?_2\ } & \boxed{\ ?_3\ } & \boxed{\ ?_4\ } \\
1 & 4 & 0 & -4 \\
-1 & 5 & 1 & -5 \\
-1 & 4 & 1 & -5
\end{bmatrix}
$$

**Present your solution the way the sample solution does:** draw the grids of squares and the network, and write each calculation next to the drawing.

a. Compute the first row of the feature map, $?_1$, $?_2$, $?_3$ and $?_4$. For each one, draw the image as a grid of squares and box the $2 \times 2$ window, then write out filter × window (multiply the matching numbers and add).

b. Apply ReLU to the feature map, then $2 \times 2$ max pooling to get a $2 \times 2$ map. Draw the feature map, the map after ReLU, and the pooled map as grids of squares. Outline the four $2 \times 2$ pooling blocks and write the max of each block.

c. Flatten the pooled map row by row into $\mathbf{a} = (a_1, a_2, a_3, a_4)$. Draw $\mathbf{a}$ as a row of 4 squares.

d. Dense layer: $z_A = 0.2a_1 + 0.2a_3$ and $z_B = a_2 + a_4$ (biases 0). Draw the network: 4 input nodes $a_1, \dots, a_4$, 2 output nodes $z_A, z_B$, and a line from each input to each output labeled with its weight (dashed for weight 0). Compute both scores.

e. Softmax: compute $p_A$ and $p_B$. Use $e^1 \approx 2.72$ and $e^2 \approx 7.39$. Add the softmax step to your network drawing: an arrow from each score to its probability node. Which class is predicted?

**Solution:** [Step-by-step solution slides](Exam3_fall26_practice1_cnn_sol.html) (click through the first-row windows, ReLU, pooling, and the dense layer).

# Problem 3. Recommendation System

A podcast app gives every podcast a 2-number embedding (number 1: news and business, number 2: comedy and stories). **These podcast embeddings were learned beforehand** by the app's model from all users' listening data, so in this problem they are **known**. Only Sarah's embedding must be computed.

| Podcast | Embedding (news, comedy) |
|:---:|:---:|
| Podcast A | (0.8, 0.2) |
| Podcast B | (0.2, 0.9) |
| Podcast C | (0.6, 0.6) |
| Podcast D | (0.1, 0.4) |
| Podcast E | (0.9, 0.8) |
| Podcast F | (0.1, 1.2) |

Last month **Sarah** listened to **Podcast E** and **Podcast F**.

a. Compute **Sarah's embedding** as the **average** of the podcasts she listened to.

b. Score every podcast with the **dot product**. Recommend the top 2 that Sarah has **not** heard.

**One week later.** Sarah played **Podcast C** and **Podcast D**; she skipped Podcast B. Three **new** podcasts were also released this week (their embeddings were also learned beforehand):

| New this week | Embedding (news, comedy) |
|:---:|:---:|
| Podcast G | (1.0, 0.5) |
| Podcast H | (0.1, 1.0) |
| Podcast I | (0.7, 0.9) |

c. Recompute Sarah's embedding as a **weighted average** of her 4 plays: older plays (E, F) count **1**, this week's plays (C, D) count **2**. Score the 5 podcasts she has not heard (A, B, G, H, I) and recommend the top 2.

d. Sarah also gave **feedback**: she **liked** Podcast D and tapped **"not interested"** on Podcast C. The app doubles the weight of a liked play and gives a "not interested" play weight **−1**. Recompute her embedding and her top 2.

::: {.callout-tip}
## Solution

a. Average each number separately over the podcasts Sarah heard:

$$
\mathbf{u} = \left(\frac{0.9 + 0.1}{2},\ \frac{0.8 + 1.2}{2}\right) = (0.5,\ 1)
$$

Sarah leans toward comedy and stories, with some news.

b. Score $= \mathbf{u} \cdot \mathbf{v} = 0.5 \times \text{news} + 1 \times \text{comedy}$, sorted from high to low:

| Podcast | Embedding | Score | |
|:---:|:---:|:---|:---:|
| E | (0.9, 0.8) | $0.5(0.9) + 1(0.8) = 1.25$ | heard |
| F | (0.1, 1.2) | $0.5(0.1) + 1(1.2) = 1.25$ | heard |
| B | (0.2, 0.9) | $0.5(0.2) + 1(0.9) = 1$ | **recommend** |
| C | (0.6, 0.6) | $0.5(0.6) + 1(0.6) = 0.9$ | **recommend** |
| A | (0.8, 0.2) | $0.5(0.8) + 1(0.2) = 0.6$ | |
| D | (0.1, 0.4) | $0.5(0.1) + 1(0.4) = 0.45$ | |

**Recommend Podcast B (1) and Podcast C (0.9).** E and F score higher, but she has already heard them.

c. **Weighted average** = (total of weight × value) ÷ (total weight).

| Podcast | Embedding | Weight | weight × news | weight × comedy |
|:---:|:---:|:---:|:---:|:---:|
| E | (0.9, 0.8) | 1 (older) | 0.9 | 0.8 |
| F | (0.1, 1.2) | 1 (older) | 0.1 | 1.2 |
| C | (0.6, 0.6) | 2 (this week) | 1.2 | 1.2 |
| D | (0.1, 0.4) | 2 (this week) | 0.2 | 0.8 |
| **total** | | **6** | **2.4** | **4** |

$$\mathbf{u} = \left(\frac{2.4}{6},\ \frac{4}{6}\right) = (0.4,\ 0.667)$$

Her vector moved toward C and D, her newest plays. Scores ($0.4 \times \text{news} + 0.667 \times \text{comedy}$):

| Podcast | Embedding | Score | |
|:---:|:---:|:---|:---:|
| I | (0.7, 0.9) | $0.4(0.7) + 0.667(0.9) = 0.88$ | **recommend** |
| G | (1.0, 0.5) | $0.4(1.0) + 0.667(0.5) = 0.733$ | **recommend** |
| H | (0.1, 1.0) | $0.4(0.1) + 0.667(1.0) = 0.707$ | |
| B | (0.2, 0.9) | $0.4(0.2) + 0.667(0.9) = 0.68$ | |
| A | (0.8, 0.2) | $0.4(0.8) + 0.667(0.2) = 0.453$ | |

**Recommend Podcast I (0.88) and Podcast G (0.733).**

d. A liked play counts double ($2 \times 2 = 4$ for D); a "not interested" play counts $-1$ (C).

| Podcast | Embedding | Weight | weight × news | weight × comedy |
|:---:|:---:|:---:|:---:|:---:|
| E | (0.9, 0.8) | 1 (older) | 0.9 | 0.8 |
| F | (0.1, 1.2) | 1 (older) | 0.1 | 1.2 |
| C | (0.6, 0.6) | −1 (not interested) | −0.6 | −0.6 |
| D | (0.1, 0.4) | 4 (this week, liked) | 0.4 | 1.6 |
| **total** | | **5** | **0.8** | **3** |

$$\mathbf{u} = \left(\frac{0.8}{5},\ \frac{3}{5}\right) = (0.16,\ 0.6)$$

Scores ($0.16 \times \text{news} + 0.6 \times \text{comedy}$):

| Podcast | Embedding | Score | |
|:---:|:---:|:---|:---:|
| I | (0.7, 0.9) | $0.16(0.7) + 0.6(0.9) = 0.652$ | **recommend** |
| H | (0.1, 1.0) | $0.16(0.1) + 0.6(1.0) = 0.616$ | **recommend** |
| B | (0.2, 0.9) | $0.16(0.2) + 0.6(0.9) = 0.572$ | |
| G | (1.0, 0.5) | $0.16(1.0) + 0.6(0.5) = 0.46$ | |
| A | (0.8, 0.2) | $0.16(0.8) + 0.6(0.2) = 0.248$ | |

**Recommend Podcast I (0.652) and Podcast H (0.616).** Podcast G (news) drops out because Sarah rejected C, the play with the most news. Podcast H (stories, close to D) comes in because she liked D. Same plays with different feedback give different recommendations: feedback tells the system how much she valued each play.
:::
